sentences.text: For Respondent(s) : Mr.
M.K. Sheoran, PP Mr. R.R. Goyal
for complainant HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR UPMAN Order 11/01/2024 1.

The instant bail application has been filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the petitioner,
who has been arrested in connection with FIR No.477/2023 registered at Police Station Sikandara,
District Dausa (Rajasthan) for the offences under Sections 143, 323, 341, 498A, 406 and 302 of IPC.

Later on, police filed the chargesheet in this matter for the offences under Sections 323, 341, 498A,
406 and 304B of IPC.
2.
It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the accused-petitioner who is father-in-law of the deceased has falsely been implicated in this case.
He submits that petitioner is suffering from cancer which is evident from his arrest memo.
Counsel submits that there is no specific allegation of harassment on account of demand of dowry soon before death.
He further (2 of 3) [CRLMB-16495/2023] submits that ingredients of Section 304B of IPC are not visible in the present case.
Counsel submits that on account of domestic disputes, the deceased consumed poison and committed suicide.
He further submits that statement of prosecution witness-Roop Singh has been recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
In his statement, it has been specifically mentioned that marriage took place in the year 2003 and deceased started living with the petitioner in the year 2014.
The petitioner is in custody since 22.09.2023.
Charge-sheet has been filed in this case and trial will take considerable time.
He also contends that further custody of the petitioner would not serve any fruitful purpose.

3. Learned Public Prosecutor assisted by learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposes the bail application and submits that there is specific allegation against the petitioner that he gave Rameshwar Prasad S/O Ramjilal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jp:2753) on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166492577/
1 beating to the deceased.

sentences.text: 4. I have considered the contentions.

5. Having regard to the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case; considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner, especially the fact that petitioner is father-in-law of the deceased and he is suffering from cancer; alleged incident took place after eight years of marriage; looking to the custody period, but without commenting anything on the merits/demerits of the case, I deem it proper to allow the bail application.

6. This bail application is accordingly allowed and it is directed that accused-petitioner - Rameshwar Prasad S/o Ramjilal shall be released on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-16495/2023] sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) together with two sureties in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) each to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court with the stipulation that he shall appear before that Court and any court to which the matter is transferred, on all subsequent dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
(ANIL KUMAR UPMAN),J DEEPA RANI-85
